manifest.name: PoS - Event Sale
manifest.summary: Link module between pos_sale and pos_event
manifest.author: Odoo S.A.

models._description: (extension) Event Registration -- POS-sold ticket status reconciliation

security.note: No own security artefacts: the model is a pure method override on event.registration; it relies entirely on the ACLs already granted by pos_event (group_pos_user CRU on event.registration) and event_sale/event.

views.note: No views and no XML/data files (xml_loc=0): the module changes only one compute method's behaviour; the registration form/list it influences are the ones declared in pos_event and event_sale.

behavioral_notes.observation: pos_event_sale's whole contribution is one re-override of _compute_registration_status (@api.depends('pos_order_id.state'), 148 py LOC, 1 method). It calls super() first, then for every registration linked to a POS order (self.filtered('pos_order_id.id')) it OVERWRITES the status with a paid-state test: if pos_order_id.state in ['paid','done','invoiced'] -> sale_status='sold', state='open'; ELSE -> sale_status='to_pay', state='draft'. This deliberately replaces the rule pos_event installed -- where any non-cancelled POS order with amount_total != 0 made the ticket immediately 'sold'/'open' regardless of payment. So a ticket on a POS order that is still draft/unpaid is now correctly 'Not Sold' (to_pay) and draft instead of prematurely confirmed. This payment-aware reconciliation is the bridge's reason to exist and is invisible to metadata (the model has 0 added fields).

behavioral_notes.element: why the bridge is needed: pos_sale's settle-from-quotation flow creates unpaid draft POS orders
behavioral_notes.observation: pos_event (without pos_sale) assumed a ticket is rung and tendered in one POS checkout, so 'amount_total != 0 => sold' was safe. pos_sale changes that assumption: it lets a cashier load a draft sale.order/quotation into the POS and settle it, and an order can carry lines and a non-zero total while still in state 'draft' until payment is validated (pos.order.action_pos_order_paid moves it to 'paid'/'done'/'invoiced'). When BOTH modules are present, an event ticket can therefore sit on a non-zero but unpaid POS order. pos_event_sale aligns event.registration.sale_status with the POS order's actual paid state, mirroring how event_sale already slaves registration status to sale_order_id.state ('sold' only when the SO is in state 'sale', else 'to_pay'). The module is the point_of_sale analogue of event_sale's sale.order rule -- hence depends ['pos_event','pos_sale'] and auto_install=true (it activates exactly when both seams are present).

behavioral_notes.element: MRO / super() ordering across event_product, event_sale and pos_event computes
behavioral_notes.observation: event.registration._compute_registration_status is overridden in a chain (event_product base default -> event_sale for sale_order_id -> pos_event for pos_order_id -> pos_event_sale here), all feeding the same stored sale_status (defined in event_product) and state (selection in event). Because pos_event_sale calls super() FIRST and then re-writes the pos_order_id-linked records, its paid-state verdict wins for POS-sourced registrations, layering on top of whatever super() (including pos_event's amount-based pass) computed. sale_status is a stored, compute_sudo, precompute field, so this recompute fires on create and whenever pos_order_id.state changes (e.g. when the order is finally tendered), flipping a ticket from to_pay/draft to sold/open without manual intervention. The interplay of these overrides is pure Python ordering and not reverse-engineerable from field metadata.

The bundled test (extends pos_event's TestUi) proves the bridge: it sync_from_ui's two POS orders each carrying an event ticket line + an event_registration_ids attendee -- order 1 with a 100.0 bank payment_ids line, order 2 in state 'draft' with empty payment_ids. After sync it asserts the two resulting event.registration records' sale_status set == {'sold','to_pay'}: the paid order's attendee is 'sold', the unpaid draft order's attendee is 'to_pay'. This is exactly the paid-vs-unpaid distinction pos_event alone could not make (it would have marked both 'sold' since both have amount_total=100). The test is the executable specification of this module.

frontend_gap3.present = false: 0 JS files, 0 XML templates, 0 OWL components, 0 registry adds, 0 patches, no asset bundles. The module is backend/ORM-only: it ships models/event_registration.py + tests/test_frontend.py and no static/ tree. The POS-side ticket-selling UX (EventConfiguratorPopup/EventRegistrationPopup/EventSlotSelectionPopup and the ProductScreen patch) is contributed by pos_event, not here -- this bridge changes only a server-side compute, so it has no client footprint. integrations_gap7 is empty.

logical_data_erm: event.registration -> pos.order (pos_order_id, related via pos_order_line_id.order_id; from pos_event)
event.registration -> sale.order (sale_order_id; from event_sale, reachable because pos_sale pulls in sale_management)
pos.order.state (paid/done/invoiced vs draft) -> event.registration.sale_status/state (this module's write)
information_flows: depends: pos_event (point_of_sale + event_product; supplies pos_order_id link, ticket-selling UI, seat broadcast), pos_sale (sale_management; supplies the settle-from-SO flow that creates non-zero unpaid draft POS orders)

side-effect: event.registration._compute_registration_status -> on create and on pos_order_id.state change, sets sale_status='sold'/state='open' iff the POS order is paid/done/invoiced, else 'to_pay'/'draft'
consequence: a ticket settled at the POS from a quotation is 'Not Sold' until the till payment is validated, then auto-confirms; mirrors event_sale's sale_order_id.state rule on the POS side
no new persistence, route, view, security or external call -- the module is a single compute re-override

capabilities: Reconcile Event Registration Status with POS Order Payment State

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: pos_event_sale is a sell-flow bridge classified chain / primary / 3.0, consistent with both of its parents (pos_event and pos_sale are each chain/primary/3.0). Its substance is a single side-effect on the in-store sell transaction: it ties the confirmation of an event-ticket sale (event.registration.sale_status='sold') to the POS order actually being paid, which is the Market-and-Sell 'accept/fulfil the order' moment realised at a till. The dominant operation it serves is the retail sale -- ringing/settling a ticket and tendering payment -- exactly the 3.5 manage-sales-orders family that point_of_sale, pos_sale and event_sale all sit in; it simply corrects WHEN the seat is counted as sold across that flow. It is primary (it is part of completing a revenue transaction, not a back-office utility) and chain (it adds value along the sell pipeline by gating order->fulfilment status on payment, the way sale.order confirmation gates downstream documents). Although the artefact it governs (event.registration) belongs to the event subsystem -- which on its own is a value NETWORK (seat-capacity mediation) -- this module touches none of that mediation: it only reads pos.order.state and writes a sold/unsold flag, so its own value logic lives squarely on the chain/selling side, not the network side. APQC 9.0 (finance) was considered because the trigger is a payment state, but rejected: the module does not manage receivables, payments or accounting entries -- it consumes the already-computed pos.order paid state to decide a SALES status, so the home is Market-and-Sell (3.0), not Manage Financial Resources.

standard_capabilities: make a POS-sold event ticket 'Sold'/open only once its POS order is paid/done/invoiced
keep a ticket 'Not Sold' (to_pay) / draft while its (possibly settled-from-quotation) POS order is unpaid
auto-flip status when the order is finally tendered (stored, precompute, compute_sudo on pos_order_id.state)
harmonise the pos_event amount-based rule with event_sale's sale-order-state rule so both channels agree
auto-install precisely when pos_event + pos_sale are both present
typical_fits: venue/box-office that both rings walk-up tickets AND settles pre-booked quotations at the same till
deposit-then-collect ticketing where a quotation is settled at the counter and only confirmed on payment
deployments that need accurate sold-seat counts excluding unpaid in-progress POS orders
common_gaps: no UI of its own -- the change is silent; there is no indicator beyond the registration's existing status field
no new refund/cancel behaviour (pos_event still owns refund-to-cancel and pos.order.state='cancel' handling)
the 'invoiced' state is treated as sold like paid/done -- bespoke to-invoice-but-unpaid policies would need an override
does not change seat-availability broadcasting (that remains pos_event's _update_available_seat regardless of paid state)

open_questions: Exact recompute timing across the override chain when sale_order_id (event_sale) AND pos_order_id (pos_event) are both set on the same registration -- which channel's rule wins after super().
Whether 'invoiced' should always count as 'sold' for to-invoice POS orders that are not yet financially settled.
How a partial refund / partial payment on a multi-attendee ticket line maps to per-registration sale_status under this rule.
Interaction with online-payment-confirmed POS orders (action_pos_order_paid timing) versus offline tendering for the status flip.
